capabilities.target: Any CRM customer record, looked up by email or account id

instructions.note: "You may look up any customer by email or account id" grants the agent unrestricted cross-customer lookup with no binding to the identity of the person emailing.
Sending is gated only on the model's own judgment of whether the customer is angry, with no structural approval step before an irreversible send.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model refusing to disclose another customer's record when the ticket requester's content induces it to look one up; a more capable model follows longer, more convincing injected goals and rationalizes exceptions.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the ticket's system-of-record owner
Scope CRM read to the authenticated requester's own account
Human approval gate (raw action review) before sending customer PII to an unverified recipient
Outbound content scan for other customers' identifiers before send
controls.decay_rationale: A separate classifier inspecting outbound content does not scale with model capability; paraphrase or encoding can get past it, though it narrows exposure meanwhile.

controls.name: Pin and hash crm_mcp and mail_mcp tool definitions
Verify crm_mcp and mail_mcp server identity (mTLS or signed identity) instead of static bearer tokens

findings.title: Lethal trifecta and confused deputy via unrestricted customer lookup and shared-account email send (TC1/TC4)

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled ticket email can request lookup of an arbitrary customer by email or account id.
Broadly-scoped CRM_SVC_TOKEN reads any customer's confidential record, not just the requester's own.
Shared MAIL_SVC_TOKEN sends the drafted reply, including the looked-up record, back to the attacker's own email address, with no structural approval.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model id or version string changes with no separate review (runtime notes state the model is upgraded with the platform, no separate review); or autonomy level/step limits are raised.

evidence.observation: "You may look up any customer by email or account id" grants unrestricted cross-customer lookup with no binding to the requester's own identity.
"If the answer is routine, send it directly with send. Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry." means sends happen without any structural approval gate.
"Never share another customer's information with the person emailing you" is the only control against cross-customer disclosure, and it is a behavioral prompt instruction.
Both crm_mcp and mail_mcp are called with static bearer tokens (CRM_SVC_TOKEN, MAIL_SVC_TOKEN) rather than per-user scoped credentials.
"CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record" and "MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account. It can send to any address" confirm broad credential scope on both capabilities.
"Every outbound email is logged to the SIEM" is detective only; it does not prevent the send.

recommendations.action: Bind the email_send recipient to the authenticated ticket requester's address from the ticketing system of record, not to any address the model infers.
Scope CRM read per request to the account associated with the authenticated ticket requester; remove the ability to look up arbitrary customers by email or account id.
Add a human approval gate with raw action review (full recipient and payload visible) before any email containing customer PII is sent to a recipient not already verified as the ticket owner.
Add an outbound content scanner that flags customer identifiers other than the requester's own before the email is sent.

findings.title: Unauthenticated, unpinned MCP tool definitions permit tampering and tool poisoning (ASI04)

attack_path.note: CRM MCP server tool definitions are not pinned or hashed and server identity is not verified.
A redefined or rug-pulled get_customer tool could be made to exfiltrate beyond the intended query.
mail_mcp is similarly unpinned and unverified; a redefined send tool could redirect or duplicate outbound mail.
A compromised or rug-pulled tool definition reaches the irreversible, shared-credential send capability.

forecast.watch_signal: A new MCP server is added to mcp.json, or any guardrail config affecting these two servers changes, without a corresponding review of auth method and definition pinning.

evidence.observation: crm_mcp and mail_mcp entries show only a URL and a static Bearer Authorization header; there is no field or note indicating tool definition pinning or hashing.
No mutual TLS, signed identity, or other server identity verification is described for either MCP server.
MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is described as a shared service account usable to send to any address, consistent with no per-call scoping that would limit the blast radius of a compromised or redefined tool.

recommendations.action: Pin and hash the crm_mcp and mail_mcp tool definitions so a silent redefinition is detected and blocked.
Replace static bearer tokens with verified server identity (mTLS or signed identity) for both MCP servers.

rating.rationale: Both findings are U/I-sourced paths into an S3 sink (confidential CRM data reaching an irreversible, broadly-credentialed email send), with the autonomy modifier applying because step and runtime limits are unset. Finding 1 (lethal trifecta / confused deputy) carries the only credited control, a behavioral prompt instruction, which holds residual at high; that control is dependent and fails under model_upgrade, longer_task_horizon, or autonomy_increase, pushing the forecast back to critical. Finding 2 (unpinned, unauthenticated MCP servers) has no declared control at all, so residual stays at the critical inherent level. The design's overall residual and forecast are therefore both critical, driven primarily by the complete absence of recipient binding, credential scoping, approval gating, and MCP definition pinning.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest schema, IaC, or source code was provided; the exact parameters accepted by get_customer and send are inferred from the system prompt and runtime notes, so confidence on precise capability boundaries is medium at best.

No evidence was provided for MCP server identity verification or tool definition pinning; both are assumed absent because the artifacts are silent on them, which could change if additional configuration is supplied.

No approval workflow configuration was provided beyond the system prompt and runtime notes; autonomy level A3 is inferred from 'do not wait for a human unless angry' together with SIEM logging as the only after-the-fact review mechanism.
